verdict.rationale: Whether a note-taking app's source is published under an open license is a fair question for this kind of product, so the axis applies. Nothing in the evidence shows a public repository or an open-source license for Capacities. The pack covers a REST API, an OpenAPI spec, MCP integration and Markdown export, and its "MCP open standard" mention refers to the protocol, not Capacities' own code. None of these make the product's source readable.
